title: Split an inherited house without a coerced waiver (real case)

source.case: r/legaladvice: 'My brothers want to keep our dad's house' (a 1/4 heir vs three siblings living in the home)
source.note: Encoded from a real thread: the poster is a one-quarter owner by intestacy; three brothers live in the house, want to keep it, and would rather buy the poster out at the lower county-assessor value than a market appraisal. A family member first asked the poster to sign away their probate rights. Positions, the no-waiver red line, and the options are from the poster's own account; no party ratified the outcome (real-case run, not a signed engagement).

presentation.situation: A parent dies without a will. You inherit a one-quarter share of the house; your three siblings live in it and want to keep it. They would rather buy you out at the low county-assessor value than a real market appraisal, and someone already asked you to just sign away your rights. What does everyone accept?

You (1/4 heir).blurb: want a fair value for your quarter, on a neutral valuation
redlines: won't sign away or accept less than half your fair share

Three brothers.blurb: want to keep the family home and pay as little as possible for your quarter

Neutral valuation.blurb: a legally clean process; won't ratify a coerced waiver
redlines: no outcome that rests on a pressured rights-waiver

market.plain: Buy you out at a market appraisal

assessor.plain: Buy you out at the lower county-assessor value

partition.plain: Force a court sale and split the proceeds

waiver.plain: Sign away your share under family pressure

presentation.outcome: The coerced rights-waiver is blocked by the neutral red line. Among the outcomes everyone can accept, the market-appraisal buyout and the low assessor buyout tie on the floor, so the tie-break by total welfare lands on the market appraisal: the siblings keep the family home, you get your quarter at a real (not lowball) value, and nobody triggers a value-destroying partition suit. Everyone gets a receipt: no one was pressured into signing their share away.
